blocks.text: At web scale, exact answers can be absurdly expensive: remembering every URL a crawler has seen, every unique visitor to a page, or the exact count of every search query. Probabilistic structures answer the same questions in fixed, tiny memory with bounded, quantifiable error — and most of them can be merged across machines, which makes them perfect for distributed aggregation.

items.title: Set up
items.text: A bit array of m bits, all 0, and k independent hash functions.

items.title: Insert x
items.text: Compute h1(x)…hk(x) mod m and set those k bits to 1.

items.title: Query y
items.text: Check its k bits. Any 0 → y was **definitely never inserted**. All 1 → **probably** inserted (bits may have been set by other items).

items.title: Size it
items.text: For n items and false-positive rate p: m ≈ −n·ln p / (ln 2)², k ≈ (m/n)·ln 2 → ~9.6 bits per item and 7 hashes at 1%.

blocks.caption: A Bloom filter in front of an LSM read

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Using a Bloom filter where a false positive is harmful (e.g. "username taken" without checking the database). Use it to skip work, and confirm positives against the source of truth.

Hash every item to a uniformly random bit string. Among n distinct items, the longest run of leading zeros you'll see is about log₂ n — seeing 20 leading zeros suggests roughly a million distinct items. One such estimate is noisy, so HLL splits items into m registers by the first few hash bits, tracks the max leading-zero run per register, and combines them with a harmonic mean. With 16,384 registers (12 KB in Redis) the standard error is ~0.81%.

items: **Mergeable:** the union of two HLLs is the register-wise max — compute daily uniques per shard and merge for monthly uniques.
Can't remove items or list them; only estimate cardinality.
Redis: PFADD key item, PFCOUNT key, PFMERGE dest src1 src2.

blocks.text: A d × w grid of counters with one hash function per row. To add item x, increment one counter in each row (column = h_i(x)). To estimate x's count, take the **minimum** of its d counters — collisions only ever add, so the minimum is the least-polluted estimate. With w = ⌈e/ε⌉ and d = ⌈ln(1/δ)⌉, the estimate exceeds the true count by at most ε·N with probability 1 − δ.

items: **Top-K heavy hitters:** process the stream, update the sketch, and keep a min-heap of the K items with the largest estimates.
Sketches merge by adding counters element-wise — compute per partition, combine centrally.
Used for trending hashtags, top queries, DDoS source detection, network flow monitoring.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The crawler keeps seen URLs in a sharded Bloom filter — a false positive only skips one page — and the analytics pipeline keeps a HyperLogLog per ad per day for unique viewers, merged into weekly and monthly numbers.
